recipes.name: Peachy Bread Pudding with Caramel Sauce
ingredients_raw: 2 cups fresh peaches - peeled, pitted and halved
4 cups French bread, torn into small pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Chop peaches and place in a large bowl; mash peaches lightly using a fork. Combine condensed milk and beaten eggs in a separate bowl; add to peaches and mix well. Stir in hot water, melted butter, cinnamon, and vanilla. Fold in bread until bread is completely moistened. Transfer mixture to the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted into the center of pudding comes out clean, about 1 hour and 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, make sauce: Combine brown sugar, butter, corn syrup, and rum in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat and simmer until just slightly thickened, 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
Remove pudding from the oven and allow to cool for about 10 minutes before serving. Serve warm with caramel sauce. Cool any leftover pudding completely and store, covered, in the refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Peachy Bread Pudding with Caramel Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This bread pudding with fresh peaches and sweetened condensed milk is topped with a warm caramel sauce spiked with rum.

video.description: Total temptation and complete comfort invite your enjoyment: From the flesh of peach releasing fresh juice to the soft hunks of torn bread soaking up a sea of rich spiced custard, and finally the endless boozy pour of rum caramel sauce pouring over ice cream and sinking into pudding, this is one sexy, unforgettable dessert date.

review.reviewBody: OMG!.. To die for!.. I made this as the recipe stated but added maybe an extra cup of French bread to use it all up and canned peaches. It was delicious; I added some whipped cream and dash of nutmeg on top for presentaion... :)

Excellent recipe and we are a family that loves bread pudding. The peaches I had were not ripe enough to use so I used canned ( not expecting to like it), boy was I wrong. I used two cans of diced peaches in heavy syrup (drained, I did not mash them as we like big chunks of peaches. In place of the hot water I used the heavy syrup I drained from the peaches which equaled a little less than 1 1/4 cup, it was plenty of liquid. I baked in a dish smaller than called for in the recipe to make it thicker and baked 1 hour and 15 mn. I left the rum out of the sauce and replaced with vanilla. This dish is superb and I will be making for a family gathering next week.

Update on my review, I've made it twice now and made a few changes that take this from a great recipe to totally amazing. I doubled the peaches to 4 cups (I used canned since they aren't in season), added a cup of fresh blueberries, used a mixture of half milk and half peach syrup instead of water, used 5 eggs instead of 3, and 6 cups of bread. It filled a 9 x 13 pan which took about an hour and 5 minutes to bake. All I can say is wow!!! Served it at a family gathering and it was huge hit. The rum caramel sauce is SO GOOD!!! We had it with vanilla ice cream, and it is a new family favorite.

This recipe was very good with a few tweaks as suggested by other reviews, which is why I gave it only 4 stars. The bread pudding itself was a decent base but definitely needed more peaches (I used 1 quart of home-canned but will use 2 next time) and at least 1 additional egg (I used 4, but will use 5 next time). I also reserved the juice the peaches were in and used that instead of water. I used 1 package of hot dog buns which turned out great as it used them up and I didn't want to go out and buy French bread.

I have to agree with the other reviews that the caramel rum sauce is the best part of this recipe - I can't say enough good things about it & if I could give the sauce 5 stars and the pudding 4, then I would. I think after I make a few adjustments this recipe will be a 5-star for sure and I will definitely be making it again & again.

I followed the recipe as well as a couple of review comments. I increased the eggs from three to 5, Added about 5 cups of bread with the crust, and I added about 3 cups of fresh chopped peaches. I did not smash them. I added about 5 cups of bread with the crusts.I baked it at 335° for 90 minutes and it was absolutely perfect. Crusty on top and well cooked in the middle. Caramel sauce turned out absolutely wonderful and both are good as leftovers. I served it for breakfast with sausage links

Great start to peach bread pudding. After reading the reviews and suggestions, I made a few adjustments myself. 

First, I roasted fresh peaches on a very lightly buttered baking sheet with a sprinkle of salt, freshly grated nutmeg and a pinch of ground cloves.

Second, I altered the custard mixture by adding an egg and some nutmeg, salt and cloves. I then, as suggested, I cut the butter in half in both the bread pudding recipe and rum sauce.

My bread, believe or not, was almost week old hot dog buns that were VERY stale (oops left them out in a bowl from a bbq last week) Perfect for bread pudding, though, as the marriage of the bread and custard didn't produce a super soggy or super dense final product. 

I covered my pudding while cooking with the exception of the last 15 minutes to toast the top. The roasted peaches added a great peachy depth to a great traditional bread pudding. Thanks for this great recipe! It was a pleasure eating it!

I just finished the recipe the flavoring is delicious, however I added 1 additional cup of water because the bread absorbed the egg batter leaving it dry. Otherwise my early thinking made it all worth it.

I made this with the following changes: used canned peaches (could not find decent fresh peaches and frozen were outlandishly expensive) then measured out a healthy 2 cups once slightly mashed up and drained). Reduced bake time to 35 minutes - custard was set in this amount of time. All other instructions were followed exactly. Excellent dessert, not overly sweet. Served with whipped cream drizzled with caramel sauce. Using a nice crusty bread results in a slightly chewy/crispy texture. In the future I might try adding brandy or dark rum to the dessert and to the caramel sauce.

Absolutely will make again - delicious - after mixing in bread I let it stand in fridge to marinate in bread - huge success at dinner party - added vanilla ice cream and Carmel sauce on top of ice cream as well

I actually only made the sauce. I saw that this was for a peachy dessert, so I figured it would be good for the Peach Cobbler Cheesecake recipe (Malissa Gray) I made for Mother’s Day. I did not have run, so I used vanilla, but then decided to add a tablespoon of bourbon since that was in the cheesecake. It was easy to make, just be careful not to cook it too long so it does not burn. I put it in the microwave for about 10 seconds just before serving in order to loosen it a bit and to get it warm, again, not wanting it to cook more. It was sweet and I could taste the bourbon just enough for a zing. It was very tasty and everyone loved it. Maybe one day I will make the bread pudding as well. I am sure it must be great as well.

A pretty good basic recipe. I did make some changes which made it a 5 star recipe. I used raisin bagels instead of Italian bread. I also used canned peaches with the natural juices and cut down the hot water to 1 cup. I also added 1/2 cup fresh blueberries. I added 5 eggs instead of 3 and 2T vanilla. I baked it for 1 hour at 350. Didn't try the caramel sauce, but did top it ice cream. My family loved it!
I left the caramel sauce on too long, but it was still delicious, just had to heat it up when I wanted to use it again.

I used canned peaches incorporating the juice with less regular milk. I used bread crusts from tea sandwiches I had made earlier. It's in the oven so I haven't tasted it. I'll use cool whip or ice cream instead of caramel sauce.
Just a little bit
Good recipe. I took the peach peels and blended them with the water and drained it through a coffee filter. It really enhanced the peach flavor in the pudding.
Absolutely delicious with home made heavy whipping cream
This is absolutely delicious. It seems to be the same recipe as this one, in case one needs to credit it. https://www.thespruceeats.com/easy-spiced-peach-bread-pudding-3051806

enjoyed it, easy, I think will add chopped nuts to it next time
